method: test-only MergeConflictProbe creates a memory (local version), then calls the production store.mergeSyncRecords with a remote record for the same id carrying a different actor clock and different content
observed: before=1 applied=0 after=2 candidate=true stored="conflict base value"
interpretation: the remote edit did not overwrite the local value (applied=0, stored value unchanged)
both versions survive (2 clocks for the same memory id)
a conflict candidate is created so the difference can be reviewed
this is the desired behaviour for device-independent data: no silent last-writer-wins
limitations: the probe calls the merge path directly; it does not travel over the transport
the review flow (choosing which version wins) was not exercised
only one memory and one conflict shape were tested
